accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow Aristotle's Rhetoric (ethos: the speaker's character and credibility; pathos: putting the audience in a frame of mind; logos: the argument itself) as used in AQA GCSE English Language 8700 (AO2 analyse language for effect, AO4 evaluate critically) and the spoken-language rhetoric unit. Techniques use standard GCSE terms (rhetorical question, anecdote, statistic, triad/rule of three, direct address). Real-world figures checked: 20 mph zones and about 40% fewer casualties (Grundy et al., BMJ 2009, London 20 mph zones, 41.9%); 23 m stopping distance at 30 mph (Highway Code). Campaign arithmetic: £240 ÷ £5 = 48 dog-weeks. Parameterised items checked at corners: p2 w 3..12 from £15..£60, p5 k*m 12..140 from 40..200 dogs, m7 w 20..60.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets slips named in AQA examiner reports on Paper 2: labelling any sad sentence as pathos (step 1 prediction on 'seven in ten… underweight', SORTWHY, m2, tag crash); treating any number as logos when it signals experience (15-years vet card, tags years); feature-spotting without effect (m6); writing about 'the reader' with no audience (step 3, OPENWHY, p4, tag never); asserted or borrowed ethos (step 4 meter, m3, tag polite); and overdone pathos backfiring (step 5 guilt-trip option, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrhet is about appeals and techniques in someone else's persuasive text: appeal sorting with per-card reasons, technique spotting in a speech, audience matching, a credibility meter and an audience-fit paragraph build. flagweigh judges an argument's evidence and reasoning tricks; flagargue plans a written argument (claim, counterclaim). Max 6-shingle similarity 3.1% (with flag_record.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: Students meet the overlap cases first and get a reason, not just a mark (the sad statistic is logos, the vet's 15 years is ethos). The credibility meter shows 10/100 for 'trust me' and 35/100 for a famous fan before the vet's 90/100. Matching openers shows that one campaign needs three different appeals. The build step shows the weak option in each pair losing the audience's trust, so they judge which appeal persuades best.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers: the underweight statistic ('pathos: it is sad'), the best opener for a council committee ('the saddest story' / 'a famous supporter'), and the strongest credibility claim ('a famous footballer' / 'everyone in town agrees'). The lab disproves each with feedback and the meter.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct messages in why(): img, who, scene, years, council, crash, story, rq, never, len, polite, stat, each naming the slip. Each lab step adds its own: SORTWHY gives a reason for every wrong bin of every card (12 messages), spot() names what the tapped line actually is plus a definition of the wanted technique, OPENWHY covers all six wrong audience pairings, CLAIMS explains each claim's credibility, SLOTS explains each weak line.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the learner audience (kid FK 3.6, adult 9.0). Terms are defined on first use (ethos = trust, pathos = feeling, logos = reason). Canvas text is 13-18 px on pale cards and wraps within each card; bins and buttons use short labels (Ethos, Line 3, Claim 2, Upper line).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (explanation overlap 0.1% at most). Kid paragraphs: the three appeals; earned ethos; five techniques with effects; audience. Adult paragraphs: GCSE objectives and key terms; named mistakes from examiner reports; how to mark overlapping appeals; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots before and after Show me at 360 px Android in light and dark. Text wraps inside each card; one sentence at a time is shown above three full-width bins so cards never shrink below 14 px; the speech lines get equal bands of the 1.35-ratio canvas. Audience bin text was 11 px on the first pass and is now 12 px. Bins are 100+ px tall tap targets and buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Sort this sentence as Logos, reason', 'Line 3: Last year we took in 412 dogs…', 'Best for: Council budget committee', 'Test claim 3: …', 'Choose: <full sentence>'. voice() updates the canvas aria-label and narration after each action; the challenge narration reads out the quoted sentence. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe clean in both themes, no console errors.
